description.narrative: The Programme MENA Feminist Power in Action for Women’s Economic Rights (Fem PAWER) will strengthen young women who face multiple discrimination1 of economic gender-based violence (E/GBV) in the MENA specific countries (Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine and Tunisia) to be the leader for change by holding duty bearers accountable and improve conditions for young women in the informal sector. This through strengthening women economic empowerment (WEE), in this Programme reflected through leadership strengthening, challenging prevailing social norms and hence gender equality, and promoting women’s economic rights (WER).

The overall goal of the Program is: Gender-responsive accountability mechanisms for WEE (Women Economic Empowerment) at multiple levels in MENA specific countries (Jordan, Lebanon, Occupied Palestinian Territories and Tunisia) are established.A framework of four interlinked and mutually reinforcing intermediate changes have been identified and designed to enable progress for gender-responsive accountability based on the needs of young women.- Outcome 1 is to establish safe and secure space for the young women and WROs to develop mobilization and advocacy strategies to hold decisions makers accountable.- Outcome 2 is addressing innovative and inclusive learning / leadership for all level of the Consortium and Program.- Outcome 3 is addressing target-led capacities in advocacy, alliance building, social mobilization and inclusive leadership for young women and the WROs that will be the Partner Organizations of the Program.- Outcome 4 is addressing the target led mobilization and advocacy interventions at multiple levels.

Young women champions for Women Economic Rights: The Programme will directly target young women with disability, and rural / refugees (20 per country and around 80 in the region) to become ‘champions’ to organise, both, country and regional networks in tackling E/GBV and promote WER. Women Rights Organisations: Local CBOs and plural in/formal networks are the most vital actor in the Programme. Approximately 12 local WROs per country will be selected representing the diversity of the WRO landscape in each country. The aim is that they further will engage young women within their communities to become engaged in parts of the Programme through subgranting.

Through different trainings, mentoring, and ongoing discussions and coordination in the network, all our capacities have grown stronger. We are now more confident in engaging with different stakeholders to push forward the women’s rights agenda. The program has evolved beautifully, and all the efforts we put in during the early years — harmonizing the network, building capacities, and conducting research — have prepared us well to advocate for women's rights.

FemPawer program adopts a bottom up approach, in which we mean having representatives of CSOs (referred to as women’s rights organisations) influencing the programme and technical support in the consortium. In this way they are more than consultative roles, they have actual influential power. This bottom up approach further includes evidence-based research, aims to contribute to the lacking knowledge base of gender responsive accountability mechanisms for E/GBV and WER for young women in the informal sector. By supporting target-led activities throughout, the Programme will ensure that discriminated young women will become advocates in their own rights, advocates that address relevant solutions and recommendations.In Year 1, PWWSD (tier 1, consortium partner), plans to identify 12 CSO (tier 2) to be part of FemPawer network in Palestine.

Following the release of a call for proposal and developing a selection criterion, PWWSD identified and selected 9 women lead grassroot organizations to be part of FemPawer network in Palestine. title.narrative: Increased influence of WRO on governments and private sector, to create space for WRO’s demands and positions on women’s economic rights, empowerment and entrepreneurship

# of times that CSOs succeed in creating space for CSO demands and positions on women’s economic rights, empowerment and entrepreneurship, through agenda setting, influencing the debate and/or movement building at subnational level

comment.narrative: The number is extracted from the baseline evaluation report. The baseline values are based on the survey conducted with young women and WROs and think tanks, and they are at subnational level.

Counting of times that that young women and WRO involved in the Programme succeed in creating space for their demands and positions on women’s economic rights and empowerment, through agenda setting and influencing the debate and/or movement building, at subnational level.

Online/offline spaces for policy and women right dialogue were created at the local level by partner oranizations in Jordan, Lebanon and Palestine.In Palestine, partners actively engaged in various dialogues, including discussions on protection, minimum wages, economic rights of women with disabilities, and ensuring decent work for women in the labor market. Additionally, they participated in dialogues concerning cooperative laws, procedures, systems, and women. Furthermore, they were part of dialogues focused on the protection system, covering social security, domestic workers, women in the informal sector, non-working women, legal protection, transparency, governance, and management of social security, with multiple partner organizations involved. Moreover, partner participation extended to campaigns led by the CEDAW coalition and the GBV coalition.

PWWSD attended the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights in Geneva during the 138th session of the UN Human Rights Council from 5 to 7/7/20223. Following this session, a development occurred: just 10 days later, the Palestinian government issued a decision published in the official gazette regarding the covenant. This decision signifies the binding nature of all laws related to the covenant in the state of Palestine, enhancing freedoms, democracy, and safeguarding the political rights of women. This achievement reflects the collective pressure exerted by civil society institutions during official and unofficial discussions on the state of Palestine's report.During the 67th session of the Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (CESCR), PWWSD participated in Geneva and presented a paper addressing the economic rights and challenges faced by women in Palestine. Various main and side events were organized, with participation from both government representatives and civil society. National reports were presented, covering topics such as violence against women, women's empowerment, and women's economic rights.

title.narrative: # of laws blocked, adopted or improved to promote women’s economic rights, empowerment and entrepreneurship

comment.narrative: The number is extracted from the baseline evaluation report.

Counting of laws, policies and strategies in Palestine that will be blocked, adopted or improved to promote gender-responsive accountability mechanisms for women’s economic rights (WER) and empowerment of women and women rights organisations’ (WORs) involved in the Programme.

Achieving tangible changes in laws and policies often requires significant time and collective efforts. While we may not have directly changed laws within the reporting period, our initiatives have played a crucial role in raising awareness among rights holders and local authorities regarding women's economic rights.Our advocacy efforts have brought various discussions to the table, including topics such as women's right to inheritance, ensuring safe transportation to work, and addressing harassment in the workplace. By engaging in dialogue and advocacy, we have initiated important conversations and highlighted the importance of addressing these issues to promote gender equality and women's empowerment.In Palestine, we successfully achieved changes to the registration procedures and reduction of registration fees for cooperatives. It's important to note that the success of this change is not solely attributable to PWWSD but to a collective effort of CSOs in Palestine.
